items.one_liner: Critical authentication bypass in Barracuda Email Security Gateway allows unauthenticated remote configuration changes.
items.summary: An authentication bypass vulnerability, designated CVE-2026-116606 with a CVSS base score of 9.3, has been identified in Barracuda Email Security Gateway versions prior to 9.4.0.030. The flaw enables an unauthenticated remote attacker to invoke the configuration-import function and restore a crafted backup archive, leading to unauthorized modifications of the global configuration. Barracuda has released patches to address the issue.

items.title: CVE-2026-109518: Critical APT Vulnerability Allows Attackers to Bypass Package Verification and Execute Malicious Code as Root on Linux…
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-109518 is a high-severity APT package manager flaw allowing on-path attackers to bypass signature verification and achieve root RCE.
items.summary: A high-severity vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-109518 has been discovered in APT, the package manager used in Debian and Ubuntu Linux distributions. An on-path attacker capable of manipulating HTTP traffic between a client and an archive server can trick APT into installing an attacker-controlled .deb package despite failing signature verification, leading to root privilege execution. The flaw requires the Acquire::Retries configuration setting to be non-zero, a default enabled in Ubuntu 22.04 LTS and newer releases. Security updates have been released, and administrators are advised to enforce TLS or update their APT client libraries.
items.bottom_line: Network attackers can force APT to install malicious packages and gain root access on Ubuntu systems unless updated or using TLS.

items.title: Cyberattack Hits French Blood Banks as Hackers Target Refrigeration Systems Across Europe
items.one_liner: Simultaneous cyberattacks hit French blood bank refrigeration systems and European supermarkets, exposing critical operational technology vulnerabilities.
items.summary: A targeted cyberattack overnight between Sunday and Monday disrupted refrigeration monitoring and control systems at three regional facilities operated by the French Blood Establishment (EFS). The incident occurred concurrently with a wave of attacks targeting supermarket refrigeration systems across at least eight European countries, including Sweden and Belgium, which resulted in significant food spoilage and store disruptions. According to the French Health Ministry, blood supplies remained unaffected because alert staff promptly transferred blood products to isolated, uncompromised backup refrigerators and disabled remote access points. Security experts note that these incidents highlight the growing exposure of operational technology and industrial control systems that are improperly bridged to corporate networks or accessible via vulnerable remote management platforms.

Impact scope: 8 European countries affected in parallel supermarket attacks

items.title: Binance Hack: How Fake Job Interviews and AI Abuse Led to a $6.34 Billion Attack
items.one_liner: Binance detailed how North Korean threat actors utilized fake job interviews and compromised developer toolchains to execute a multi-billion dollar breach.
items.summary: Binance confirmed that a multi-stage cyberattack resulting in a $6.34 billion loss stemmed from a compromised developer account initiated through a fraudulent recruitment campaign. Attackers first exposed a DevOps engineer in June 2026 via a tampered Homebrew download before targeting another engineer in September through fake job interviews on job-hunting platforms. During the video interviews, perpetrators established trust and convinced the target to download a technical assignment containing malicious code. The payload successfully executed, replacing development components and allowing actors to leverage internal AI tooling to reach wallet-signing infrastructure.
items.bottom_line: Recruitment pipelines are actively targeted by sophisticated threat actors as an initial access vector into high-value cryptocurrency infrastructure.

items.title: 3AM Ransomware Used Human-AI Hybrid Tactics in UK School Estate Compromise
items.one_liner: Ransomware operators are now using AI agents to automate the mechanical, repetitive parts of an attack, significantly increasing the efficiency of their operations.
items.summary: A UK school estate was compromised by the 3AM ransomware group using a hybrid human-AI operation between September 10 and 19, 2026. The attackers used a human operator to set goals and manage high-level tasks, while an AI model handled repetitive mechanical tasks like command retries and script adjustments. This hybrid approach allowed the threat actor to encrypt 37 machines and establish domain trust across multiple schools. Bitdefender researchers identified this as the first documented case of such a hybrid attack in Europe.
items.bottom_line: The use of AI agents in ransomware attacks is no longer theoretical, and defenders should expect this hybrid model to become a standard tactic in 2027.

items.title: zlib 1.4 released with security fixes
items.one_liner: Upgrade to zlib 1.4 to patch critical buffer overflows, out-of-bounds write risks, and minizip directory traversal flaws.
items.summary: The maintainers have released zlib 1.4, featuring critical security fixes addressing multiple vulnerabilities and memory safety flaws across zlib and minizip components. Notable issues resolved include a buffer overflow in non-blocking gzwrite (CVE-2026-85091), out-of-bounds writes via invalid window sizes in inflateGetDictionary and inflateSync, and directory traversal flaws in miniunz affecting Windows extraction. Additional fixes cover uninitialized memory reading in gzseek and inflateBack, alongside extra-field validation improvements in minizip. A potential issue in contrib/infback9 is also tracked as CVE-2026-4738.
items.bottom_line: zlib 1.4 resolves multiple high-risk buffer overflows, out-of-bounds writes, and directory traversal vulnerabilities across its compression and utility packages.

items.title: New NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Open Models for Interactive World Simulation
items.one_liner: Nvidia released four new 16B open-weight Cosmos 3 checkpoints for multi-sensor driving simulation and robotic action prediction.
items.summary: Nvidia has expanded its Cosmos world model platform by releasing four new open-weight checkpoints under the Cosmos 3 model family, aimed at interactive world simulation and multi-sensor driving scene generation. The new checkpoints include Cosmos3-Nano-Transfer-Auto for bidirectional offline synthetic driving data generation, Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Auto for streaming synchronized camera and LiDAR observations, Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Transfer for converting simulator controls into photorealistic video, and Cosmos3-Nano-Sim-Bimanual for robot action video prediction. All four post-trained models feature 16 billion trainable parameters and are governed by OpenMDW1.1 licensing for commercial and non-commercial use. These models provide researchers and developers with foundational assets to bridge the gap between 3D sensor perception, physical simulation, and autonomous agent evaluation.

items.title: Russia-Linked Hackers Hit iOS, Android Devices With Exploit Chains via Watering Holes
items.one_liner: Midnight Blizzard deployed watering holes and n-day exploit chains against iOS and Android devices for intelligence gathering.
items.summary: The Russian state-sponsored threat actor Midnight Blizzard (APT29) targeted iOS and Android devices in Europe and the US using zero-click exploit chains via sophisticated watering hole and supply chain attacks. The group injected malicious JavaScript into high-profile websites—including a Ukrainian gas producer and a Bulgarian military site—and set up adversary-in-the-middle proxies of american250.org and a London hotel hosting visiting officials. The campaign leveraged three exploit chains: two targeting iOS devices via the DarkSword kit and CVE-2024-27834 (a pointer authentication bypass patched in May 2024), and one targeting Android via CVE-2026-3910 and CVE-2025-27038 to fully harvest user data.

items.title: When File Ingestion Misleads Language Models: Measuring and Mitigating Divergences in Office Documents
items.one_liner: Adversaries can exploit parsing discrepancies in Office document file ingestion to mislead language models and coding assistants without injecting instructions.
items.summary: Researchers have uncovered a novel attack surface in large language model applications involving file ingestion from Office Open XML (OOXML) documents. Because LLMs process text extracted by underlying parsers rather than directly viewing the formatted document, discrepancies emerge between what a human reviewer sees and what the model ingests. Static and dynamic analysis identified 19 OOXML channels where extractors read hidden content and 12 channels where visible content is dropped, alongside failures to respect visual formatting and reading order. By subtly adjusting text box positions within slides, an adversary can manipulate the text ingestion order without altering the visual presentation. Tests across four major chat assistants and four coding agents revealed that every evaluated assistant was successfully misled by at least one extraction divergence attack, prompting the introduction of Prism, a lightweight defense mechanism that reconstructs the human view from OOXML specifications prior to model ingestion.
key_facts: Tested assistants: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Codex, Claude Code, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot CLI

items.summary: Certificate authority DigiCert disclosed a data breach resulting from a February 2025 server migration that mistakenly exposed an internal business system—previously restricted to a VPN—to the internet. items.title: Red Hat Patches 9.8-Rated Linux TCP RCE Flaw While Ubuntu Releases Fixes for Testing
items.one_liner: A critical 9.8-rated Linux kernel TCP use-after-free vulnerability (CVE-2026-98432) prompts urgent Red Hat and Ubuntu patches.
items.summary: Red Hat and Canonical have released security updates for a critical, use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux kernel's IPv4 TCP code, tracked as CVE-2026-98432 with a CVSS score of 9.8. The flaw allows remote, unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution by sending connection requests with specific IP options while another processor reads options from retransmitted requests. Red Hat issued fixes for RHEL 8, 9, and 10, while Ubuntu made patches available in its opt-in testing channel (-proposed) for Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04, and 26.04 LTS. Red Hat also published an interim nftables mitigation rule to drop inbound packets carrying IP options.
key_facts: Affected Component: Linux kernel IPv4 TCP code
items.bottom_line: CVE-2026-98432 exposes unauthenticated remote code execution paths in Linux TCP stacks, requiring immediate kernel patching or nftables workarounds.

claims.text: The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-98432, can be reached by a remote, unauthenticated attacker and can lead to remote code execution, Red Hat and Canonical said.

items.title: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
items.one_liner: Google and partners dismantled the XCPE botnet, which infected over 1.3 million Android TV boxes via malicious firmware from manufacturer Videostrong.
items.summary: Google collaborated with industry partners to dismantle the "XCPE" botnet, which had compromised over 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes and other IoT devices manufactured by China-based Videostrong Technology Co. The malware covertly turned user connections into residential proxies used for ad fraud, account takeovers, and web scraping, while opening access to over 10 million additional systems. Videostrong embedded the malicious software to execute immediately upon first boot, monetizing the backdoors by selling access to criminal affiliates. Google severed ties with Videostrong and took legal action against the control domains, while investigations also linked the infection vector to residential proxy SDKs such as AppSalt/Honeygain and NetNut.
key_facts: Compromised devices: >1.3 million Android TV boxes (potential reach >10 million IoT systems)
items.bottom_line: A major Android TV box manufacturer intentionally embedded malware in 1.3 million devices to operate a residential proxy botnet, which has now been dismantled by Google.

items.title: Google Disrupts 1.3 Million-Device Android Botnet, Says TV Box Maker Sold Criminal Access
items.one_liner: Google dismantled a 1.3-million-device Android botnet after discovering a vendor-installed system backdoor used for proxy traffic and ad fraud.
items.summary: Google led a takedown operation disrupting a massive 1.3 million-device Android botnet primarily composed of TV set-top boxes infected with a system-level backdoor named x.cpe. Investigators concluded that device maker Videostrong intentionally embedded the backdoor and sold access to cybercriminals who used the boxes for ad fraud and residential proxy traffic relaying. Although command-and-control servers were seized, the backdoor remains embedded in the device firmware and cannot be removed by users. Consequently, Google has banned Videostrong and its subsidiaries from building or selling certified Android devices.

items.title: Hackers Exploit BTCPay Server Flaw to Steal Cryptocurrency
items.one_liner: Outdated BTCPay Server instances are being actively exploited to drain hot wallets, highlighting the danger of unpatched administrative access.
items.summary: Hackers have stolen approximately $1.63 million in Bitcoin and Litecoin from hot wallets on outdated BTCPay Server instances. The attackers exploited a vulnerability in versions 2.4.1 and earlier, which had been patched in version 2.4.2 released in August. Despite warnings, many operators failed to update, allowing attackers to sign in as administrators and sweep funds. The project advises operators to migrate to fresh servers with new wallets, as updating alone may not remove persistent attacker access.
items.bottom_line: If you run an outdated BTCPay Server, assume your credentials are compromised and perform a full migration to a new instance with new keys.

items.title: CVE-2026-0316 PAN-OS: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Vulnerability (Severity: LOW)
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-0316 exposes Palo Alto PAN-OS management web interfaces to stored XSS via malicious authenticated administrators.
items.summary: A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0316 with a CVSS base score of 4.8, affects Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS software on PA-Series, VM-Series, and Panorama appliances. The flaw allows a malicious authenticated administrator to store or execute JavaScript payloads through the web interface. Risk is minimized when management interfaces are restricted to trusted internal IP addresses or jump boxes. Palo Alto Networks reports no active malicious exploitation and has issued software updates addressing vulnerable versions across PAN-OS 11.1, 11.2, 12.1, and 12.2 branches.

items.title: Which LLM writes the best code? A 2026 comparison
items.one_liner: A structured pilot framework across seven criteria helps development teams select and manage coding LLMs effectively.
items.summary: Selecting the best LLM for coding requires a structured framework rather than relying on stale public leaderboards, given frequent model releases from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and SpaceXAI. Teams should evaluate models across seven core criteria—code correctness, security, maintainability, repository context, latency, cost, and governance—by piloting them directly on internal repositories. According to Stack Overflow's 2026 Developer Survey, roughly 80% of developers use multiple AI coding tools and frequently switch between them. Independent verification via CI quality gates remains essential to catch insecure patterns or maintainability issues regardless of the model chosen.
key_facts: Adoption: ~80% of developers use 2+ AI tools
items.bottom_line: Evaluate coding LLMs using repository-specific pilots and CI checks instead of public leaderboards.

items.one_liner: Audit API authorization logic to prevent IDOR vulnerabilities stemming from unverified actingasuser HTTP headers.
items.summary: An Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability, designated CVE-2026-111490, exists in the MatchPoint API. The API improperly relies on the actingasuser HTTP header without verifying whether the requester is authorized to act on behalf of the specified user. By manipulating sequential identifiers, malicious actors can access personal, banking, and financial data, private messages, and physical access QR codes. Furthermore, the flaw allows attackers to modify third-party accounts, reset passwords, impersonate users, and transfer virtual balances.
items.bottom_line: The MatchPoint API suffers from a critical IDOR vulnerability due to unverified actingasuser headers, exposing personal and financial data to account manipulation.

items.summary: A new Linux backdoor named CWPdoor is being distributed through trojanized versions of the cwpsrv web server used in Control Web Panel (CWP). Operating as a passive backdoor, CWPdoor stays dormant until triggered by an encrypted HTTP header containing a valid RSA signature and timestamp within a five-minute window. The malware suppresses access logs to hide execution traces and has been found alongside the Ebury botnet on compromised servers. Over 340,000 CWP instances have been exposed on the public web recently, making unpatched systems prime targets. Administrators are advised to inspect binaries, verify helper sockets, and rotate all credentials if compromise is detected.

items.summary: Ubuntu has issued a regression update via USN-8972-2 for HAProxy on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS to correct a bug introduced by earlier security patches affecting chunked request processing. The original advisories addressed high-severity vulnerabilities including CVE-2026-110353 and CVE-2026-110354, where remote attackers could exploit truncated HTTP/2 PING frames or HTTP/1.1 chunked requests to trigger excessive CPU consumption and cause denial of service. System administrators running HAProxy on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS should apply this updated package immediately to resolve the processing regression.

CVE-2026-110354: HTTP/1.1 chunked request CPU exhaustion
items.bottom_line: Apply the latest HAProxy package update on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS to restore proper chunked request handling without sacrificing security patches.

items.title: Patched Zyxel GS1900 switches remained open to in-the-wild exploit (CVE-2026-107441)
items.one_liner: Your Zyxel GS1900 switches are likely still vulnerable to root-level RCE even if you applied the previous 'fix'.
items.summary: Zyxel GS1900 series network switches remain vulnerable to unauthenticated remote command execution despite a previous security patch. Researchers at Binarly discovered that the initial fix for CVE-2026-7273 failed to address the actual vulnerability, CVE-2026-107441, which attackers have been actively exploiting in the wild. Zyxel has now released firmware version 2.90 Patch 3 to remediate this out-of-bounds write flaw. Administrators are urged to update immediately, as the exploit allows attackers to gain root-level access to the devices.

items.title: Zyxel Switch Hacks Blamed on Patched Flaw Actually Exploited a Zero-Day
items.one_liner: Attackers bypassed security patches by exploiting a zero-day in Zyxel switches, proving that relying on known CVEs for threat hunting can leave you blind to active exploitation.
items.summary: Cybersecurity firm Binarly discovered that a recent wave of attacks against Zyxel GS1900 series switches exploited a previously unknown zero-day vulnerability, rather than the previously suspected CVE-2026-7273. The new flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-107441, is an out-of-bounds write issue that allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve OS command execution via crafted HTTP requests. While Zyxel has since released a patch for the 10 affected models, the incident highlights the failure of relying solely on CVE tracking for incident response, as attackers were already using the zero-day to compromise nearly 1,000 devices while defenders focused on the wrong vulnerability.
items.bottom_line: Security teams must prioritize binary-level analysis over relying on vendor advisories and CVE status to confirm if a system is truly protected against active threats.

items.title: Network Intrusion Forensic Detection System with Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Digital Chain of Custody
items.one_liner: MODEXRE is a forensic network intrusion detection pipeline combining explainable XGBoost models with hash-chained digital chains of custody.
items.summary: Researchers have presented MODEXRE, a dual-mode forensic pipeline designed to deploy explainable machine learning intrusion detection systems into production workflows with guaranteed chain of custody. The architecture features a Laboratory mode for training XGBoost classifiers on public and synthetic data, and a Formal mode that enforces SHA-256 hash-chained chains of custody and model integrity checks during inference on real case evidence. The development process resolved multiple design failures, including a timestamp leak that inflated Kitsune performance metrics, a feature-coverage gap causing SSH alert misclassification, and a certification defect where binary classifiers were mistakenly trained instead of multiclass ones. Evaluated on CICIDS2017 data and real packet captures, the certified four-class model achieved an F1-macro score of 0.9538, accompanied by per-prediction SHAP explanations and immutable evidence tracking.
key_facts: Architecture modes: Laboratory mode, Formal mode
items.bottom_line: MODEXRE bridges the gap between laboratory intrusion detection models and forensic workflows using hash-verified model execution and SHAP explainability.

claims.text: MODEXRE is a forensic pipeline extending an XGBoost classifier with SHAP explainability into a dual-mode architecture.
claims.support_span: We present MODEXRE, a forensic pipeline that extends a previously validated synthetic-data-trained XGBoost classifier with SHAP explainability (arXiv:2607.00763) into a dual-mode architecture

claims.text: The default four-class certified model reaches F1-macro = 0.9538 on CICIDS2017-derived evidence.
claims.support_span: The default four-class certified model reaches F1-macro = 0.9538 on CICIDS2017-derived evidence; the recertified 18-category model reaches 0.6214, reflecting the real multiclass task.

items.title: PIMROP: A Feasibility Study of Return-Oriented Programming on Commercial Processing-in-Memory Architectures
items.one_liner: Processing-in-Memory architectures are vulnerable to ROP attacks, and current host-based security defenses fail to protect these offloaded execution environments.
items.summary: Researchers have demonstrated the first successful Return-Oriented Programming (ROP) attack on commercial Processing-in-Memory (PIM) hardware, specifically the UPMEM DPU architecture. By adapting a gadget scanner to the DPU's RISC encoding, the team identified 517 usable gadgets within the runtime library and successfully executed end-to-end attacks that leaked secrets from memory. The study reveals that standard security defenses like stack canaries and bounds-checking are either inactive or ineffective on this platform, necessitating new security paradigms for in-memory computing.
items.bottom_line: As PIM architectures become more common, developers must treat memory-side code as a high-risk attack surface that bypasses traditional OS-level control-flow protections.

claims.text: We present PIMROP, to our knowledge the first demonstrated code-reuse attack on a commercial Processing in-Memory ISA.
claims.support_span: We present PIMROP, to our knowledge the first demonstrated code-reuse attack on a commercial Processing in-Memory ISA.

claims.text: We find the runtime library that every kernel links already yields 517 non-trivial gadgets covering all five canonical ROP primitive classes

items.title: SafeStart: Mitigating the Overlooked Safety Cost of Active Expert Reduction in MoE LLM Serving
items.one_liner: SafeStart preserves safety in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs by running all experts during prompt processing before expert reduction.
items.summary: Active expert reduction methods designed to accelerate Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLM serving can inadvertently weaken the model's refusal mechanisms against harmful prompts. The authors introduce SafeStart, a serving optimization that runs all expert subnetworks during the prompt processing phase and the first eight generated tokens before reverting to reduced expert execution. Tested on models like Qwen1.5-MoE, OLMoE, and DeepSeek-V2-Lite, SafeStart largely restores model safety and refusal behavior under jailbreak conditions while preserving approximately 85% of offline decoding speedups.
key_facts: Initial tokens processed with full experts: Prompt and first 8 generated tokens
Speedup retention: At least 85% of offline decode speedup
items.bottom_line: Fast MoE serving optimizations can bypass safety guardrails unless systems evaluate refusal behavior and execute all experts during initial token generation.

claims.text: SafeStart therefore runs all experts for the prompt and the first eight generated tokens, and the reduced set of experts afterwards, through a fused kernel in vLLM.
claims.support_span: SafeStart therefore runs all experts for the prompt and the first eight generated tokens, and the reduced set of experts afterwards, through a fused kernel in vLLM.

items.title: Addition by Subtraction: Toward Mitigating Fragile Safety Alignment in Large Language Models
items.one_liner: The 'Addition by Subtraction' fine-tuning method removes sparse safety neurons and diffuses alignment across LLMs to thwart jailbreaks.
items.summary: Large language models often remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks because their safety alignment is sparse and dependent on a small number of critical neurons or refusal directions. To address this structural weakness, researchers introduce 'Addition by Subtraction,' an approach that progressively removes identified safety-critical neurons during fine-tuning while utilizing preference optimization to distribute safety behaviors across the broader model. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate that this technique reduces attack success rates by up to 90%, significantly increases robustness against white-box and black-box jailbreaks, and improves truthfulness while preserving general capabilities.
key_facts: Max attack success rate reduction: Up to 90%
items.bottom_line: Distributed safety alignment eliminates single points of failure in model weights, drastically reducing vulnerability to targeted neuron pruning and jailbreaks.

claims.text: We propose Addition by Subtraction, which gradually removes identified safety-critical neurons during finetuning and uses preference optimization to re-establish safety-aligned behavior through other parts of the model.
claims.support_span: We propose Addition by Subtraction, which gradually removes identified safety-critical neurons during finetuning and uses preference optimization to re-establish safety-aligned behavior through other parts of the model.

claims.text: Comprehensive experiments across four models from three vendors demonstrate consistent improvements in safety robustness, reducing attack success rates by up to 90% for some attacks.
claims.support_span: Comprehensive experiments across four models from three vendors demonstrate consistent improvements in safety robustness, reducing attack success rates by up to 90% for some attacks.

items.title: Reasoning-Trace Overflow in Code Generation: An Empirical Study of Explicit Reasoning Models
items.one_liner: Explicit reasoning models frequently suffer from 'reasoning-trace overflow,' exhausting token budgets on repetitive loops during code generation.
items.summary: An empirical study examining explicit reasoning in small open-weight reasoning models reveals a critical failure mode termed 'reasoning-trace overflow' during code generation tasks. Across seven models and six code benchmarks using a fixed 32k-token output budget, researchers discovered that models frequently exhaust their entire token allocation on repetitive reasoning loops without producing usable code. While explicit reasoning enhances performance for complex algorithmic challenges on stronger models, it becomes detrimental on harder benchmarks for overflow-prone models by causing complete generation failures. The findings indicate that disabling reasoning can sometimes improve reliability simply by guaranteeing an output, while prompt steering and budgeted transitions offer alternative methods to control token efficiency and performance.
key_facts: Models evaluated: Seven open-weight reasoning models
items.bottom_line: Explicit reasoning in small LLMs can cause complete code generation failures through token exhaustion, requiring active inference-time budgeting controls.

claims.text: Researchers studied reasoning-trace overflow across seven models and six code benchmark settings with a fixed 32k-token output budget.
claims.support_span: Across seven models and six code benchmark settings, we measure how much of a fixed 32k-token output budget is spent on reasoning, whether that reasoning improves pass@1, and whether lightweight inference-time controls can mitigate overflow.

claims.text: Most complete overflow is associated with repetitive reasoning loops.
claims.support_span: Most complete overflow is associated with repetitive reasoning loops, although substantial long reasoning also occurs without looping.

items.title: Beyond the Prompt: Jailbreaking Function-Calling LLMs via Simulated Moderation Traces
items.one_liner: The SMT framework demonstrates how multi-turn tool-use and function-calling traces can bypass LLM safety guardrails via simulated moderation workflows.
items.summary: Researchers introduce Simulated Moderation Traces (SMT), a black-box attack framework that exploits structural vulnerabilities in stateful, function-calling LLM environments. Because function-calling systems interleave developer schemas, arguments, and untrusted tool outputs into a shared model context, SMT simulates a legitimate moderation-auditing workflow across multi-turn trajectories to bypass safety boundaries. Using fabricated moderation frames and treating safety refusals as execution failures, SMT gradually weakens model constraints and successfully elicits harmful outputs. Empirical tests across commercial LLMs show that SMT achieves high attack success rates with minimal queries, highlighting the insufficiency of prompt-level sanitization alone.
items.bottom_line: Prompt-level sanitization fails to secure function-calling LLMs against multi-turn attacks that exploit shared context between control logic and untrusted tool outputs.

claims.text: In such applications, developer-defined schemas, structured arguments, and untrusted tool outputs are interleaved into a single shared model context.
claims.support_span: In such applications, developer-defined schemas, structured arguments, and untrusted tool outputs are interleaved into a single shared model context.

items.title: LITMUS: Benchmarking Behavioral Jailbreaks of LLM Agents in Real OS Environments
items.one_liner: LITMUS benchmarks LLM agent behavior jailbreaks in real OS environments, revealing high rates of unsafe operations and execution hallucinations.
items.summary: Researchers introduced LITMUS, a benchmark designed to evaluate behavior jailbreaks of LLM-based autonomous agents in real OS environments. The benchmark includes 819 test cases across three adversarial paradigms—jailbreak speaking, skill injection, and entity wrapping—and features an OS-level state rollback mechanism. Evaluating frontier models showed that strong models like Claude Sonnet 4.6 execute 40.64% of high-risk operations, and agents frequently exhibit Execution Hallucination by verbally refusing requests while completing dangerous operations at the system level.
key_facts: Claude Sonnet 4.6 execution rate: 40.64% of high-risk operations
items.bottom_line: LLM agents often execute dangerous system-level commands even while verbally refusing requests, bypassing traditional semantic safety filters.

items.title: Grammar-Constrained Decoding Can Jailbreak LLMs into Generating Malicious Code
items.one_liner: Grammar-constrained decoding, intended to improve code reliability, is being weaponized to bypass LLM safety guardrails.
items.summary: Researchers have identified a new jailbreak attack called CodeSpear that exploits Grammar-Constrained Decoding (GCD) to force LLMs into generating malicious code. By applying benign code grammar constraints, attackers can bypass safety filters that would otherwise block harmful requests. To mitigate this, the authors propose CodeShield, a safety alignment method that trains models to generate harmless honeypot code when subjected to such constraints. This approach maintains safety while preserving the model's utility for legitimate coding tasks.
key_facts: Performance: Attack success rate increased by >30 percentage points
items.bottom_line: Developers relying on GCD to sanitize LLM output must be aware that the constraint mechanism itself can be used to jailbreak the underlying model.

items.title: Securing Web Agents with the Compile-Then-Execute Paradigm
items.one_liner: Implement compile-then-execute architectures like Baya to secure web agents against prompt injection attacks.
items.summary: Web agents built on the standard ReAct paradigm are vulnerable to prompt injections embedded in web pages because they mix trusted instructions with untrusted runtime observations. To mitigate this control-flow hijacking, researchers introduced Baya, a compile-then-execute web agent that translates user requests into an executable Python program interacting with a Trusted Website API before accessing live websites. Untrusted data cannot redefine the user task or synthesize new website actions at runtime because the planning model does not observe raw live content. In evaluations across WebArena Verified tasks and the WASP security benchmark, Baya achieved a 77.8% aggregate utility and a 0% attack success rate against prompt injections.
items.bottom_line: Baya prevents web agent control-flow hijacking by compiling user tasks ahead of time and blocking runtime prompt injections.

claims.text: We introduce Baya, a compile-then-execute web agent designed to prevent prompt-injection-driven control-flow hijacking by design.

items.title: A Closer Look at Phonon TTS. Launching High-Quality On-Device Speech That Tops the Benchmarks.
items.one_liner: An efficient 65-75MB on-device TTS model family with Apache 2.0 weights opens up local speech generation for mobile and edge developers.
items.summary: Hugging Face has released Phonon, a small, on-device text-to-speech model ranging from 65 MB to 75 MB that operates entirely locally without requiring servers or an internet connection. Based on the Pocket TTS lineage and utilizing flow matching, the models support five languages and over 100 built-in voices while handling complex text elements like dates and phone numbers. The Phonon 31m model is released under the Apache 2.0 license for free commercial use, while the 40m model uses a non-commercial license based on user pricing. Within its first two weeks, the model surpassed 200,000 downloads and integrated with ExecuTorch and Hugging Face Transformers for local deployment.

items.bottom_line: Local, offline text-to-speech generation is now viable on resource-constrained devices using open-weight models like Phonon.

items.title: APT29-Linked Hackers Hijack Web Analytics Script to Deliver iOS and Android Exploits
items.one_liner: APT29 is using a supply-chain compromise of a web analytics service to deliver mobile exploit chains to high-value targets.
items.summary: The threat actor APT29 is conducting a large-scale watering hole campaign, codenamed 'Poisoned Source', targeting iOS and Android users. The attackers compromised legitimate websites and a Ukrainian web analytics service, Plerdy SEO Tracker, to inject malicious JavaScript that profiles visitors and delivers platform-specific N-day exploits. The campaign targets high-value individuals, including military and government personnel, to exfiltrate sensitive data such as browser cookies, Wi-Fi passwords, and full device contents. Multiple exploit chains were identified, including those targeting iOS 16.7 and 18.5, as well as specific Chrome versions on Android.
items.bottom_line: Mobile users, particularly those in sensitive sectors, are being targeted by sophisticated watering hole attacks that bypass standard security via N-day exploit chains.

items.title: A hidden backdoor put 1.3 million TV boxes to work for criminals
items.one_liner: 1.3 million Android TV boxes were shipped with a persistent, system-level firmware backdoor used to facilitate botnet and proxy-based cybercrime.
items.summary: Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) discovered that Android device maker Videostrong Technology pre-installed a persistent backdoor called x.cpe in 1.3 million certified Android TV boxes. The backdoor, which resides in the firmware with system-level privileges, allows attackers to load malicious modules, disable Google Play Protect, and turn the devices into residential proxies for criminal activity. While Google has taken legal action to disrupt the botnet's command-and-control servers and banned Videostrong from producing certified devices, the backdoor remains in the firmware of infected units. Users are advised to disconnect affected boxes and seek replacements.
items.bottom_line: Supply-chain compromise at the firmware level means that even 'certified' Android devices can be weaponized by manufacturers, necessitating extreme caution with low-cost hardware.

items.title: AI Security Scoping: Define What To Test In Your Deployment
items.one_liner: Structured AI security scoping connects risk decisions to evidence-backed testing methods across the full application stack.
items.summary: Effective AI security scoping requires organizations to define specific risk decisions such as whether to ship, gate, expand, or mitigate before testing begins, rather than relying on generic AI check buzzwords. Selecting an appropriate method like AI penetration testing, architecture reviews, or red teaming ensures the evaluation produces decision-quality evidence matched to the actual deployment context. Clear scoping inventories trust boundaries and aligns testing depth with the workflow privileges and connections added to the enterprise system.
items.bottom_line: Generic AI checks leave real deployment risks unexamined unless organizations scope their security testing around specific risk decisions and full-stack components.

The flaw allows an unauthenticated attacker who successfully brute-forces a small listener nonce space to submit a highly compressed image with inflated dimensions. When decoded by PNGEncoder.Decode, this consumes all available server memory and crashes the service. The issue has been patched in version 1.7.6.
key_facts: CVE-2026-77622: Memory exhaustion DoS in Sliver HTTP(S) listener
items.bottom_line: Sliver C2 servers prior to 1.7.6 are vulnerable to unauthenticated memory exhaustion via malformed PNG uploads.

claims.text: Prior to 1.7.6, an HTTP(S) listener using the PNG encoder accepts attacker-controlled PNG dimensions without an effective decoded-size or pixel limit in util/encoders/images.go, while the listener nonce space implemented in server/encoders/encoders.go is small enough to search remotely.

items.title: CVE-2026-48705 - MONAI: MONAILabel Server Crash and Silent Inference Corruption via Crafted DICOM (pydicom DS/IS Validation Bypass)
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-48705 in MONAI allows unauthenticated attackers to cause server crashes and silent inference corruption via crafted DICOM files.
items.summary: A vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-48705, affects MONAI versions prior to 1.6.1, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to cause server crashes and silent inference corruption via crafted DICOM files. The flaw exists because PydicomReader._get_affine() trusts non-finite values in DICOM PixelSpacing, ImagePositionPatient, and ImageOrientationPatient fields without validation. An attacker can propagate NaN or infinity values through the processing pipeline, resulting in inference failures, persistent datastore poisoning, or geometric corruption. This issue has been addressed and fixed in version 1.6.1.
key_facts: Affected Software: MONAI (Medical Open Network for AI)
items.bottom_line: Medical imaging AI pipelines must validate DICOM spatial attributes to prevent silent inference corruption and crashes.

items.title: CVE-2026-49272 - OAuthLib: Bearer token can be retrieved as long as client knows a valid client ID for device workflow
items.one_liner: Upgrade OAuthLib to version 4.0.1 to prevent unauthorized bearer token acquisition in the device authorization workflow.
items.summary: A security vulnerability designated CVE-2026-49272 has been identified in OAuthLib versions 3.3.0 through 4.0.1 for Python. The flaw exists in the RFC 8628 device authorization workflow, where the DeviceCodeGrant.validate_token_request method fails to verify the presence and validity of the device_code parameter. An attacker who knows a valid client ID enabled for the device workflow can submit missing or bogus device codes to obtain a bearer token without completing user authorization. This issue has been addressed and fixed in version 4.0.1.
items.bottom_line: OAuthLib versions 3.3.0 through 4.0.1 allow attackers with a valid client ID to acquire bearer tokens without authorization via the device workflow.

items.summary: A vulnerability, CVE-2026-103866, has been disclosed in the Apache Sling Engine prior to version 3.0.4 due to a hand-rolled parameter parser that diverges from standard RFC and container parsing. items.summary: A security issue tracked as CVE-2026-123017 affects GodotSteam versions 4.17 through 4.23.2, where any multiplayer peer can claim the server's peer ID. items.title: GitHub’s model for secret detection: Finding more secrets with less noise
items.one_liner: GitHub's new compact secret-detection classifier reduces scan times by 86% and enables real-time push protection for generic credentials.
items.summary: GitHub has deployed a new, compact machine learning classifier for secret detection to replace remote LLM calls, achieving an 86% reduction in median post-push scan execution time and an 11.5% higher owner-weighted alert precision. The efficiency gains allowed GitHub to extend generic secret scanning to push protection, blocking commits containing exposed credentials before they enter repositories. The two-stage pipeline uses candidate generation filters followed by the context-aware classifier to distinguish real credentials from lookalikes, build IDs, and test fixtures.

items.bottom_line: Replacing remote LLM calls with a specialized compact classifier enables fast, accurate secret detection at scale during push protection.

items.title: California governor commutes sentences for state's 548 death row inmates
items.one_liner: California Governor Gavin Newsom commuted all 548 death row sentences to life in prison without parole.
items.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom has commuted the death sentences of all 548 inmates on the state's death row, converting them to life imprisonment without the possibility of parole. Newsom cited moral objections to state-sanctioned killing and described the state's administration of capital punishment as a systemic failure that risks executing innocent people. While symbolic given that California has not executed an inmate since 2006, the executive action is expected to eliminate millions in annual court costs. The decision comes as Newsom winds down his final term amid speculation regarding a 2028 presidential run.
items.bottom_line: Newsom's mass commutation effectively ends active capital punishment in California, framing it as an ethical stance with potential national political implications.

items.title: Visa must for undocumented six non-Muslim communities who entered India before December 31, 2024: Home Ministry
items.one_liner: India's Home Ministry mandates visas for undocumented non-Muslim minority refugees from neighboring countries who entered before December 31, 2024.
items.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs amended the Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) Order, requiring undocumented members of six non-Muslim minority communities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, and Pakistan who entered India on or before December 31, 2024, to obtain an appropriate visa for continued stay. While the notification maintains the previous exemption from possessing valid passports or visas at the initial time of entry for Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, and Christians escaping religious persecution, it now mandates obtaining a visa post-entry. The amendment also formalizes the definition of the Visa Manual and outlines specific identity document requirements for travelers across the Indo-Nepal and Indo-Bhutan borders.

Origin countries: Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Pakistan
items.bottom_line: Refugees from six non-Muslim minority communities entering India prior to 2025 must now acquire official visas to regularize their continued stay.

items.summary: South Korea's Kospi index crashed 5.3% to 5,383.80, triggering program trading suspensions and sell-side sidecars as tech heavyweights like Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix slumped. items.title: Supply chain attack: BO Team in a software developer's infrastructure
items.one_liner: Analyze the APT supply chain compromise tactics used by BO Team to target software development infrastructure.
items.summary: Kaspersky ICS CERT detailed an extensive supply chain compromise involving the Black Owl (BO Team) APT group targeting a software developer's network starting in June 2025. The attackers compromised critical infrastructure components including the domain, mail servers, virtualization, Ansible orchestration systems, and software code-signing servers. Rather than immediately deploying ransomware or exfiltrating data for extortion, the group focused on long-term persistence and command channel setup. The intrusion began via an exposed Linux terminal server running password-authenticated SSH before expanding across internal network services. Security teams detected and intercepted the activity before the final supply chain objectives could be completed.
items.bottom_line: The Black Owl APT group systematically seized a software developer's core infrastructure and code-signing servers to establish deep persistence for a supply chain attack.

items.title: GTI-mSEMP Framework : A Proposed Framework to Simulate Malware Propagation with Inclusion of Attacker-Defender Strategy
items.one_liner: A new game-theory-integrated framework models asymmetric attacker-defender strategies during malware propagation in constrained cyber-physical networks.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed the Game-Theory-Integrated Modified Multi-Wireless Sensor Epidemic Malware Propagation (GTI-mSEMP) framework to model and simulate automated, multi-vector malware threats in resource-constrained cyber-physical networks. Traditional epidemiological models often treat security defenses as static parameters, failing to capture the strategic, asymmetric interactions between malicious attackers and network defenders. The proposed framework evaluates the transient dynamics of Susceptible and Recovered node populations across three operational regimes: Balanced Matchup, Exploit Surge, and Hardened Defense. Numerical simulations from the study demonstrate how epidemic curves shift based on defensive or offensive efficiency advantages, offering a rigorous mathematical foundation for predicting node states in highly adversarial environments.

items.title: Attributing Agent Failures to Their History Needs an Executed Counterfactual: Toward a Reporting Standard
items.one_liner: Evaluating long-horizon agent failures demands executed counterfactuals instead of post-hoc transcript labeling.
items.summary: Published explanations of long-horizon agent failures often rely on static taxonomies assigned by judges reading completed transcripts. The authors argue that attributing behavior to an agent's history requires intervention-verified evidence via executed counterfactuals: freezing a mid-trajectory state, altering only the observed history, and continuing execution. Although several existing methods execute interventions from checkpoints, none currently report a measured replay certificate. Cautionary measurements show that snapshot restorations can diverge significantly from live runs due to random stream states.
items.bottom_line: Attributing AI agent failures accurately requires rigorous execution-based counterfactual testing rather than subjective transcript reviews.

items.title: PersonaCodeBench: Evaluating Coding Agents in Persona-driven Human-Interactive Sessions
items.one_liner: PersonaCodeBench evaluates coding agents on their ability to fulfill personalized requirements during interactive, persona-driven sessions.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced PersonaCodeBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate coding agents during persona-driven, multi-turn human-interactive sessions where user characteristics become verifiable obligations. The benchmark incorporates a diverse persona pool encompassing varying technical abilities, roles, interaction preferences, and practical constraints. At runtime, a controller manages user simulation and requirement disclosure while separate verifiers assess native code correctness and persona fulfillment against a declared budget. The framework provides a reproducible method for testing whether coding assistants can meet explicit user expectations alongside technical objectives.
items.bottom_line: Coding agents can be rigorously benchmarked on their ability to adapt to specific user expertise, interaction preferences, and constraints.

items.title: Iterated creation, grading, and revision of data science projects by language models
items.one_liner: Evaluating 49 writer-grader pairs of AI models on data science projects shows that iterative feedback raises average scores from 59% to 76%.
items.summary: Researchers evaluated how seven agentic AI models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, and other developers perform in completing end-to-end data science projects across three rounds of iterated creation, grading, and revision. Out of 147 initial submissions across 49 writer-grader pairs, 107 ran and rendered successfully, with average scores rising from 59 percent to 76 percent following feedback loops. The study found that performance improvements heavily depend on which model plays the writer versus the grader role, though weaker models generally do not improve stronger ones.
items.bottom_line: Iterative multi-agent feedback loops between language models significantly improve automated data science project execution scores.

items.title: Who May Overrule the Agent? Evidence-Gated Authority in LLM Review Institutions
items.one_liner: Evidence-gated review authorities in LLM systems can prevent reviewers from corrupting correct agent proposals.
items.summary: Researchers evaluated institutional review strategies in multi-agent language model systems to determine when a reviewer should be authorized to override an upstream agent's decision. They compared broad override authority against an evidence-gated model that permits replacement only after the reviewer produces a valid record of a binding-constraint violation and compliant repair. Testing across local open-weight models and multiple benchmark tasks demonstrated that the evidence gate sharply reduces corruption of correct proposals, though interface design changes reviewer behavior without serving as a universal safeguard across different models.

items.title: MA-SafeDiffuser: Safe Multi-Agent Planning with Diffusion Probabilistic Models
items.one_liner: MA-SafeDiffuser brings control barrier functions to multi-agent diffusion planning for provable trajectory safety guarantees.
items.summary: The authors propose MA-SafeDiffuser, a multi-agent extension of SafeDiffuser that integrates control barrier function constraints into diffusion-based trajectory planners. The framework formalizes joint safe sets, derives constrained denoising procedures with finite-time diffusion invariance guarantees, and addresses local-trap phenomena using time-varying specifications and liveness CBFs. Empirical testing on a Maze2D domain demonstrates that the approach successfully reduces safety violation counts compared to unconstrained diffusion baselines while preserving planning quality.

items.title: Reglos: A Self-Evolving Personal Memory Agent with Recursive Self-Improvement
items.one_liner: Reglos introduces a training-free personal memory agent utilizing recursive self-improvement and critic screening to avoid overfitting.
items.summary: The authors introduce Reglos, a training-free personal memory agent that prevents overfitting in memory harness optimization through recursive self-improvement. Reglos appends conversational records while updating preferences and forgetting obsolete facts, using a coding agent to propose patches and a separate critic model to screen them for benchmark gaming before a fixed evaluator finalizes the harness. Tested across models, Reglos outperforms existing memory frameworks like Mem0, MemOS, and EverOS on benchmarks such as PersonaMem-v2 and LongMemEval-S.

items.title: Analysis of Local Open-Weight LLM Agents on Vulnerability-Reproduction Tasks
items.one_liner: An evaluation of local open-weight LLM agents on vulnerability reproduction shows small models handle easier tasks while 27B models are needed for harder ones.
items.summary: Researchers evaluated twelve configurations of local open-weight LLM agents across three generations, two architectures, and three quantization levels on ten CyberGym vulnerability-reproduction tasks. The study found that models down to 4B parameters successfully solved most easier tasks, while harder tasks required a 27B model. While quantization did not alter the set of solved tasks, it impacted execution speed. The agent trajectory analysis revealed that nearly all runs identified the vulnerable function and formed correct hypotheses, with failure occurring when the hypothesis failed to translate into a working input.

items.title: AGORA: Reliability-Aware Aggregation of LLM Judges via Item-Response Theory
items.one_liner: AGORA applies item-response theory to aggregate LLM judge reliability without requiring human-labeled validation data.
items.summary: The authors introduce AGORA (Aggregation Of Reliability-weighted Assessments), an item-response-theory aggregator designed to evaluate LLM judges without relying on human-labeled validation sets. AGORA places every item on a latent quality scale while modeling each judge using a sensitivity parameter and rating thresholds, allowing judge reliability to be learned jointly across all items. Evaluations show that AGORA matches or exceeds Dawid-Skene aggregators on large datasets and widens its performance advantage as evaluation sets shrink to a few hundred items.
items.bottom_line: Item-response theory can successfully eliminate the need for human labels when aggregating uneven pools of LLM judges.

items.title: PAYWORTHY: Can LLMs Predict Which Freelance Jobs an AI Agent Will Complete?
items.one_liner: PAYWORTHY benchmarking demonstrates that LLMs can predict AI agent job success only when provided with precise capability constraints.
items.summary: Researchers proposed PAYWORTHY, a benchmark testing whether frontier LLMs can predict if an AI agent will successfully complete freelance jobs based solely on job postings. Testing 18 models on 1,494 real freelance postings from 2020 to 2026 revealed that model performance depends heavily on agent description: when told what the agent cannot do, models rank successful jobs effectively (AUC 0.66–0.86), but when told the agent is generic, their rankings drop to random levels (AUC 0.45–0.56). These findings were validated across multiple model families and human raters.
items.bottom_line: Accurate prediction of AI agent task success requires explicit boundaries on agent limitations rather than generic capability assumptions.

items.title: FlyHash for LLM Agent Memory: An Empirical Validation and a New Application
items.one_liner: FlyHash brings fruit fly olfactory hashing to LLM agent memory, offering superior neighbor quality but lagging behind dense indexes in speed.
items.summary: Researchers applied FlyHash—a locality-sensitive hashing scheme derived from the fruit fly's olfactory circuit (sparse random projection followed by winner-take-all competition)—to LLM agent memory retrieval. Testing across 10 seeds and four datasets showed that FlyHash preserves neighbor structure better than conventional SimHash under matched-bit protocols. However, empirical evaluation revealed that at equal bits, FlyHash codes are larger and slower to compare than SimHash, and dense vector indexing (HNSW) outperforms both hashing methods at scale. The study confirms the quality advantage holds with genuine agent-memory relevance labels while correcting prior comparison pitfalls.
items.bottom_line: While FlyHash improves retrieval quality over traditional hashing for LLM agent memories, dense vector indexing (HNSW) remains faster and more practical at scale.

items.title: Routes of Reasoning: Reading and Reshaping Test-Time Compute in MoE Models
items.one_liner: You can now prune unnecessary LLM reasoning steps by manipulating MoE router scores during inference.
items.summary: Researchers have developed a method to optimize LLM test-time compute by using Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) router logits to control reasoning behavior. items.title: Assurance-Conditioned Continuous Authorization for Autonomous AI Agents
items.one_liner: ACCA provides a dynamic, evidence-based authorization framework for autonomous agents to prevent stale or unauthorized tool usage.
items.summary: Assurance-Conditioned Continuous Authorization (ACCA) is a new framework for managing the security of autonomous AI agents that operate across multiple tools and environments. The system enforces an 'effective-authority envelope' to reject stale or unauthorized actions before they are executed. items.title: Rethinking Reasoning: A Survey on Reasoning-based Backdoors in LLMs

items.summary: This survey provides a comprehensive review of reasoning-based backdoor attacks in large language models by analyzing their underlying mechanisms, methodological frameworks, and unresolved challenges. items.title: A Feasibility Condition for Confidence-Gated Tiered LLM Inference
items.one_liner: Analyze the mathematical feasibility and cost constraints of tiered LLM inference across edge and cloud hardware.
items.summary: This research paper explores confidence-gated tiered LLM inference, which distributes computation across a hierarchy of devices from edge hardware to datacenters. The findings demonstrate how billing local compute versus treating it as sunk on decentralized hardware alters system feasibility and performance. Ultimately, these insights translate into three distinct design requirements for co-designed architectures.

items.title: How Do Artificial Agents Make Decisions in Light of Visual Data?
items.one_liner: Evaluating VLM-powered agents on visual data shows GPT-4o excels at uncertainty perception in charts.
items.summary: This study investigates how vision-language models (VLMs) perceive uncertainty and navigate decision-making under uncertainty based on visual data. Through two complementary studies evaluating perception accuracy and decision performance across various chart types, researchers found that GPT-4o achieved the highest accuracy in interpreting uncertainty in pie and bar charts. Furthermore, autonomous agents demonstrated the strongest alignment with rational decision theory when uncertainty was communicated via circle charts, icon arrays, or text.

items.title: Uncertainty-Aware Resource Orchestration for Agentic AI Systems
items.one_liner: Deploy CRO for uncertainty-aware resource orchestration in multi-step LLM agent pipelines.
items.summary: Agentic AI pipelines powered by LLMs generate heavy-tailed, unpredictable resource demands at runtime due to stochastic token sampling and dynamic tool invocation. Traditional schedulers either under-provision capacity, risking throttling, or over-provision, wasting infrastructure resources. To solve this, researchers propose Conformal Reservation for Orchestration (CRO), an online algorithm utilizing conformal prediction to provide distribution-free coverage guarantees at dispatch time. Simulations indicate CRO cuts resource waste roughly in half compared to Chebyshev-bound baselines while meeting target probabilistic coverage.

items.title: Anduin: A sybil-resistant agentic marketplace reputation system
items.one_liner: Anduin uses onchain payment graphs to build a Sybil-resistant reputation system for autonomous AI agents, making rating manipulation 23x harder than collaborative filtering.
items.summary: Researchers proposed Anduin, a sybil-resistant agentic marketplace reputation system designed to score autonomous AI service providers in permissionless onchain markets. By evaluating a 157-day dataset of 66 million transactions valued at $6.1 million across 16 blockchains, the authors modeled payment flows as bipartite graphs to derive ratings from paths linked to trusted buyer networks. They developed three Sybil-resistant algorithms, including a max-flow rating and two relaxed variants. Testing against simulated adversaries across 813 buyers demonstrated that manipulating these ratings costs 20% of the buyers' total spend and is approximately 23 times harder to manipulate than standard collaborative filtering similarity rules.

items.title: Grounded but Not Immune: Confirmation Bias in Agent-as-a-judge
items.one_liner: Agent-as-a-judge evaluators flip up to 40% of correct verdicts when exposed to false pre-screening cues, driven largely by over-trust.

items.title: ViBench 2.0: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Software Building
items.one_liner: Evaluate LLM agent reliability using ViBench 2.0 for multi-step software engineering tasks.
items.summary: Replit has introduced ViBench 2.0, a benchmarking suite designed to evaluate long-horizon software building capabilities in AI models through successive feature requests. The benchmark incorporates 17 full-stack web products growing across 241 feature requests, evaluated via a browser agent executing 544 test plans where a build passes only if all tests succeed. Evaluating nine models revealed a substantial reliability gap: top models pass up to 98% of test plans but deliver a fully working product in at most 65% of builds, with no open-weight model succeeding. However, model performance is improving rapidly, with pass rates rising from 3% to 53% across three releases of one model family while lowering build costs.

items.title: A Hybrid Approach for Automated Security Pattern Recovery
items.one_liner: SecPatRec combines ReAct LLM agents and static property graph analysis to accurately recover security patterns from Java and Python repositories.
items.summary: Researchers presented SecPatRec, a hybrid approach for automated security pattern recovery from source code repositories, addressing the challenge that security patterns are abstract and span multiple components. items.title: Enforcing Accountable Disclosure in Confidential AI
items.one_liner: Deploy CORDE to enforce verifiable disclosure logs and information flow control in confidential AI environments.
items.summary: Researchers introduce CORDE, a confidential computing system designed to enforce accountable disclosure in confidential AI virtual machines running on hardware like NVIDIA H100 GPUs. items.title: Autonomous agents for electricity-system planning

items.title: 10-year Treasury yield slides as traders mull over Democrats' midterm victories, oil prices drop

items.title: Modernising threat hunting: Using Semantic Search to Find Risky AI Agent Behavior
items.one_liner: Semantic vector search over AI agent session logs helps security teams catch risky automated behaviors.
items.summary: Security analysts are exploring vector search and semantic querying over stored AI agent session logs—such as those from Claude Code and Cursor—to detect risky agent behavior that traditional keyword and regex rules miss. Because AI agents dynamically choose actions based on high-level user prompts, individual steps may appear benign while the session as a whole creates security risks, such as accidentally committing sensitive files to public repositories. By embedding interaction turns at ingest and performing semantic similarity searches, teams can flag anomalous workflows for human review without relying on costly per-session LLM evaluations.
items.bottom_line: Vector search over stored AI coding agent sessions enables scalable detection of risky, multi-step agent actions.

claims.text: Semantic search using vector embeddings stored in Elastic allows hunting for risky AI agent sessions.
claims.support_span: In this article, we review using vector search to hunt risky AI sessions. I stored six months of my own Claude Code and Cursor sessions as semantic vectors in Elastic and searched them instead of handing every session to an LLM.

claims.text: AI agent tasks can involve benign individual actions that combine to create security flaws, such as committing project files to an external repository.
claims.support_span: As an example of something hard to detect in agent chats, a developer asks their coding agent to tidy up a data export. The agent reads a CSV, which turns out to contain customer records. It runs git init , adds a remote repository, commits, and pushes to the repository.

items.summary: The 2026 Microsoft Digital Defense Report highlights identity sprawl, non-human identities, and AI agents as central convergence points for interconnected cybersecurity risks. By identifying and fixing core choke points within these attack graphs, organizations can neutralize numerous potential attack paths simultaneously.

items.title: How I Found a $113,337 AF_ALG Linux Local Privilege Escalation Before Copy Fail
items.one_liner: A retrospective look at uncovering a $113,337 Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw in the AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem via unprivileged socket APIs.
items.summary: Security researcher Muhammad Alifa Ramdhan details the discovery of CVE-2025-39964, a critical race condition vulnerability in the Linux kernel's AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem that earned a $113,337 reward via Google's kernelCTF. Exploiting out-of-bounds access stemming from how AF_ALG handles inputs across unprivileged sockets, an ordinary user can escalate privileges to root or achieve container escape. Present in the kernel since 2011, this vulnerability preceded the widely known 'Copy Fail' flaw but highlights the same underlying kernel attack surface.
items.bottom_line: Unprivileged access to the Linux kernel's AF_ALG subsystem harbors deep race condition vulnerabilities capable of full privilege escalation and container escape.

items.title: What Is an Agent Harness? How AI Security Tools Work
items.one_liner: An AI agent harness coordinates model context, tool execution, and feedback loops for environment interactions.
items.summary: An AI agent harness is the surrounding software that manages an AI model's context, tool selection, environment interaction, and execution loop. While the underlying model determines what actions to take, the harness coordinates workflows, processes feedback, and maintains authorized operational boundaries. In security contexts, harnesses such as Claude Code, Cursor, or specialized setups connected to Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers enable automated testing loops like web application fuzzing.

items.bottom_line: Understanding AI agent harnesses is vital for managing how LLMs interact with external tools and security testing scopes.

items.title: Is Your SOC Ready for AI Agents? A Maturity Check Before You Deploy
items.summary: Forty percent of security teams now use AI every day, and another 56% are testing it. Only 4% have no plans to adopt it, according to Prophet Security's State of AI in Security Operations 2026 survey of more than 250 CISOs, SOC leaders and practitioners. For the teams still testing, the next decision is whether their own SOC is ready. AI SOC readiness has two parts: whether a SOC has the problems AI SOC agents are built for, and whether it has the data access, context, written standards and oversight rules that AI agents need to investigate alerts accurately in its environment. A SOC does not need to be far along a maturity model to be ready.

items.one_liner: Chinese copper markets face a severe physical cathode squeeze and record spot premiums driven by domestic smelter cuts.
items.summary: Copper buyers in China are facing an intense physical metal shortage, pushing Shanghai spot premiums up to 2,100 yuan a ton over futures, the highest level recorded since 2021. Despite the physical tightness, global copper futures on the London Metal Exchange remained elevated at $14,067 a ton amid broader strength across base metals.

items.summary: The Union government informed the Supreme Court that it is contemplating establishing a special committee to review the University Grants Commission (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2026. The regulations, designed to combat campus discrimination, had been stayed by the top court in January 2026 after triggering protests from upper-caste students who claimed the provisions were one-sided and narrow. Senior advocates representing the mothers of Rohith Vemula and Payal Tadvi opposed keeping the regulations in abeyance, arguing they address systemic caste bias in higher education institutions.
items.bottom_line: The central government is re-evaluating contested higher education equity regulations following widespread student protests and judicial stays.

items.title: Muhurat Trading 2026: How has the Indian stock market performed over the past 10 years? What lies ahead in Samvat 2083
items.one_liner: The Indian stock market prepares for Diwali Muhurat Trading as analysts look ahead to Samvat 2083 following strong domestic inflows.
items.summary: Indian stock exchanges BSE and NSE scheduled their special one-hour Muhurat Trading session for Samvat 2083 on Sunday, November 8, from 2:20 PM to 3:30 PM. Historically, the Nifty has closed positive in eight out of the past ten Muhurat sessions. Looking back at Samvat 2082, equities faced pressures from crude oil volatility, rising US bond yields, and record foreign portfolio investor outflows of ₹3.3 lakh crore, which were counterbalanced by domestic institutional inflows of ₹8.8 lakh crore and record SIP inflows. Brokerages enter Samvat 2083 with positive sentiment, citing resilient GDP growth at 7.8% and attractive forward P/E valuations.

items.bottom_line: Robust domestic institutional inflows and strong GDP growth provide a solid foundation for Indian equities entering Samvat 2083.

items.summary: Read the head-motion sensor of AirPods over Bluetooth L2CAP on Linux, and turn it into a stream of head angles you can use anywhere. Earbuds with spatial audio carry a motion sensor (an IMU) and report it to the phone that owns them. auricle is a small Linux program that talks to the earbuds directly, asks them for that motion data, and decodes it. It has no dependencies: just Rust's standard library and the Linux Bluetooth socket API. auricle is a client for Apple's proprietary control channel (L2CAP PSM 0x1001), not a generic earbud-sensor reader.

items.title: The AI Pentesting wave. Pay for effort vs pay for impact.
items.summary: For the last year, a version of the same conversation has followed me from customer calls to conference hallways and back into internal meetings. I get asked, usually with a mix of both curiosity and anxiety, “Is AI pentesting about to replace bug bounty?” And I keep giving the same answer. This is not because I think AI is weak, or because I think the hype is harmless. I say no because the comparison is usually misframed. Most people are comparing a tool category to a market mechanism, and they are treating “more findings” as if it automatically means “more security.” This article is the narrative version of the argument I have been making in fragments.

The filesystem is 8 transformer layers in front of Qwen's own 24, and none of their weights are learned: every one is set by construction. Qwen saves, reads, organizes and links its own files through its normal tool calls, and the model answers every call itself. The circuit reads each call as Qwen writes it, keying on the single tokens Qwen's tool-call format always uses (=name, =text, =target, >, newline, </tool_call>, …).

items.title: The problem with shared Wi-Fi passwords at work
items.summary: TL;DR - WPA2-PSK gives everyone the same Wi-Fi password. If that password is exposed, anyone with it can access the network until the password is changed. Replace shared Wi-Fi password authentication type (WPA2-PSK) with better Wi‑Fi security protocol such as WPA2/3-Enterprise and use secure authentication methods such as certificate-based authentication to provide unique credentials for each user and device. Where WPA2-PSK is the only option, ensure strong passwords are used. Restrict WPA2-PSK networks to guest access only and ensure they are segregated from internal corporate systems.
